title: FRM-CIM: Full-Digital Recursive MAC Computing in Memory System Based on MRAM for Neural Network Applications
problem: Computing-in-memory systems experience severe MAC operation delay increases as precision improves, limiting scalability and practical deployment for neural network inference.
motivation: Energy-efficient neural network inference requires fast multiply-and-accumulate operations to enable practical edge device deployment with minimal latency and power.
method: The paper proposes a full-digital recursive MAC (FRM) scheme using spin-transfer-torque MRAM and segmented bit-line arrays that perform parallel recursive read and addition operations. This approach eliminates analog components while reducing MAC latency to 3.5ns (8-bit) and 4ns (16-bit) through bit-level parallelism. An adaptive layer-wise pruning method is applied to maximize neural network compatibility.
key_novelty: Full-digital recursive MAC using segmented bit-line arrays in STT-MRAM to achieve sub-4ns latency MAC operations across multiple precision levels.
contributions: Fast FRM scheme reducing MAC delay to 3.5ns (8-bit) and 4ns (16-bit) precision
FRM-CIM system architecture with adaptive layer-wise pruning for neural network compatibility
4.3x throughput improvement and 2.6x energy efficiency gain over state-of-the-art
Validation on MNIST (96.65%) and CIFAR-10 (82.7%) image recognition
limitations: Specific limitations and practical scalability constraints not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Computing-in-memory for energy-efficient neural network inference
